note: Videogame adaptation, not Captain's Log rules. Book (Core p.141 (CL p.137)): Captain's Log does not use equipment; its conversion notes for Star Trek Adventures list standard issue as uniform, communicator, tricorder, and a sidearm (phaser type-1 or type-2 for security and senior officers), with no stats. Every stat below is PROTOTYPE TUNING for the future videogame systems and may be rebalanced freely. Keep all balance numbers here, never in UI or combat code.
worldImageNote: Isometric prop PNG drawn when the item is dropped. The file is already the stacking cell: large gear is 128×192 (32×32, four per tile), small gear is 64×96 (16×16, sixteen per tile). The board draws file pixels ÷ 4. Inventory UI uses icon.
stackSizeNote: Derived from the picture, not authored. Width and depth are the opaque picture in design pixels (the stacking cell). Height is the painted block above that picture's floor diamond.
sourceTypeNote: Provenance for development only, never shown to the player. sourceType is where the item itself comes from; statsSourceType is where its stats come from. Values: 'captains-log' (book rules or content), 'adaptation' (our videogame version of a book element), 'original' (our own system). Every item here is named in the book without stats (CL pp.39-40: communicators, standard and specialty tricorders, type-1 phaser sidearms, medical tricorder, medkit, engineering toolkit; Core p.141 (CL p.137): uniform, communicator, tricorder, type-1 or type-2 phaser). All stats, slots, and the automatic loadout are adaptation.
categoryHighlightNote: World hover outline colour for dropped items by category (exploration GroundLootView). Presentation only.
equipSlotsNote: Approved for the exploration inventory UI (2026-10-17): body, sidearm, scanner, communicator. null = carried in the bag, not equipped.

statDisplay.note: Display order and labels for stats. 'bands' turns a numeric value into a word on screen; the number stays the tuning value. Weapon stats (severity, range) are not kept here: combat/weapons.json owns them, linked by itemId, and the display reads them from there.
